title: Cross-runtime session protocol and SDK samples for progressive invocation and typed responses
creator: Ava Chen
description: Define and ship language idiomatic SDK samples and a lightweight session protocol for cross-runtime progressive invocation. Goals: enable TypeScript/Python/Go clients to open an invocation session, receive typed incremental events (tokens, tool calls, structured JSON fragments), support resumable reconnects, and demonstrate compatibility shims for older clients.
acceptance_criteria: Session protocol draft (v0.1) documented in RFC-style doc with wire-level events and reconnect semantics
TypeScript, Python, and Go SDK example repositories contain minimal working examples illustrating: startSession(), sendInput(), onEvent(handler), graceful reconnect, and finalResult()
Examples show typed-schema enforcement for structured outputs and a fallback path for legacy text-only clients
Integration test that runs small local runtime shim to validate token streams, tool call event, and structured JSON emission per the protocol
API docs updated in the SDK reference and console quickstarts with runnable snippets
implementation_notes: Design decision: use a hybrid websocket + event-framing model instead of pure SSE to support bidirectional control messages and fast reconnect negotiation
Framing: each event is a newline-delimited JSON envelope with 'type' field: 'token', 'structured', 'tool_call', 'checkpoint', 'error', 'session_meta'
Reconnect strategy: client provides last_seen_event_id and optional KV-cache prefix; server may reply with 'checkpoint' events to allow fast dedupe/caching
Typed structured outputs: include 'schema_id' and 'fragment_index' on 'structured' events; example uses small JSON-Schema pointers embedded in session_meta

Compatibility shim: include a negotiation handshake where 'features' array advertises 'streaming_structured_v1' and older clients without it will fall back to 'text_stream' which converges tokens into a final text payload
Trade-offs: websocket increases client complexity for lightweight browser embed vs SSE; we mitigate by providing a thin browser wrapper that exposes an EventSource-like interface
Kernel/runtime considerations: keep per-session KV cache descriptors short (<=256 bytes) and avoid sending full model weights or large serializer payloads on handshake
Observability: emit session-level metrics (events/sec, tool_call_count, reconnects) tied to token billing so we can detect expensive reconnect loops
dev_tasks: Draft session protocol doc and review with runtime and SDK leads
Implement thin browser wrapper in TS SDK to present EventSource-like API backed by websocket
Add resumeSession() and session metadata plumbing to Python and Go SDKs
Create integration harness that simulates mid-stream tool_call and reconnects
Author unit/integration tests and CI job to run the harness on PRs
Write guide 'Migrating from text-only streaming to typed progressive sessions' for console docs
